# NOAA versus Kalshi (generated by analysis/compare_forecasts.py; do not edit by hand)

### Accuracy on test days

Same contracts for every model. The blend was fit on train days only.

105 days, 630 contracts, 1000 day-level bootstrap replicates. Lower is better; brackets are 95% intervals.

| Model | Days | Contracts | Brier [95% CI] | Log loss [95% CI] |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Calibrated NOAA | 105 | 630 | 0.1229 [0.1143, 0.1318] | 0.3917 [0.3640, 0.4236] |
| GEFS ensemble | 105 | 630 | 0.1450 [0.1337, 0.1569] | 0.6558 [0.5371, 0.8024] |
| Climatology | 105 | 630 | 0.1685 [0.1533, 0.1823] | 0.5588 [0.5071, 0.6125] |
| Kalshi midpoint | 105 | 630 | 0.1091 [0.1010, 0.1172] | 0.3408 [0.3168, 0.3643] |
| Kalshi + NOAA blend | 105 | 630 | 0.1090 [0.0996, 0.1185] | 0.3371 [0.3083, 0.3649] |

Blend weights in log-odds: Kalshi 1.192, NOAA 0.085.

### Does disagreement carry signal?

A slope of 0 means no signal. For outcomes, 1 would mean moving Kalshi fully to NOAA. Later move is the Kalshi midpoint at noon on the target day minus its noon cutoff value.

| Split | Outcome surprise on disagreement | Later Kalshi move on disagreement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| train | -0.000 [-0.139, 0.147] | -0.038 [-0.143, 0.065] |
| test | 0.009 [-0.276, 0.297] | -0.105 [-0.268, 0.067] |
